page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory footprint totals 64 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic workloads, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across diverse computing tests. The instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 1504.0 and a multi-core score of 9335.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21808.97. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 93.7 GB/sec, while write bandwidth stabilizes at 48.12 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the configuration achieves 14.74 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 13.61 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. On compact language models such as a 135M parameter architecture, text generation reaches 277.2 tokens per second, but scales down to 13.19 tokens per second on 7B models.

The instance includes neither integrated local storage nor hardware graphics accelerators, requiring attached network persistent disks for system volumes and file retention. Given its balanced resource distribution, the instance provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded applications that do not demand AVX-512 vector acceleration or ultra-high local IOPS. Typical workload deployments include medium-scale database instances, web and API application servers, continuous integration pipelines, and general corporate software stacks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, driven by an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor across 8 physical cores. With a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides steady middle-tier compute capabilities, delivering a multi-core Geekbench score of 9335.0 and Redis SET operations reaching 14.74 million operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 93.7 GB/sec. The configuration lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, making it dependent on networked persistent disks for file storage. Supported by cryptographic instruction flags including AES and SHA-NI, n2d-standard-16 functions effectively as a stable environment for production web services, enterprise backends, CI/CD runners, and relational database hosting.
